summary: Chhime Rigdzing (1922–2002) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held a post at Visva-Bharati University.

Chhimed Rigdzin (1922–2002) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under and taught Choying Khyabdel, conducted research at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (~1953–1957), and served as Professor of Tibetan at Visva-Bharati University (~1957–1987).

Chi Chen Ho works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ho studied under traditional teacher Hsuan Hua, earned a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles under Robert E. Buswell Jr. in 2010, and served there as a teaching assistant.

Chi-chiang Huang specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. Huang completed a PhD at the University of Arizona in 1986 under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao, also studying under Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Chan studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, completed a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1993, and served as a teaching assistant at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Chia Theng Shen (1913–2007) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions and held a post at the Buddhist Association of the United States (~1964–2007).
Chiara Policardi works in Indology and religious studies. She studied under supervisor Raffaele Torella (attested 2016) and was a PhD candidate at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2014–2016).
Chie Ikeya works in history and archaeology. She earned a PhD at Cornell University in 2006, where she studied under David K. Wyatt.
Chien Y. Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies. Hsu studied under traditional teacher Zhenhua (attested 2013) and doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura (until 2011) and James B. Apple.

Chien-hsing Ho specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Ho served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and held a post at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

Chienlin Lee earned a PhD at National Dong Hwa University (2009–2020) in Tibetology and other fields. Lee taught at National Taitung University (2020–2022) and National Dong Hwa University (2022–2023), followed by a postdoctoral fellowship at Academia Sinica in 2023.
Chiew Hui Ho specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ho completed a PhD at Stanford University (2004–2013) and served as Discipline Chair at the University of Sydney in 2013.

Chih-fu Li works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Li served as Director of the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2007) and later as its honorary director (attested 2026, retired December 26, 2006).

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. Tseng earned a PhD at McMaster University under James A. Benn, also advised by Nobuyoshi Yamabe and Canshan Cheng, and held faculty posts at Fo Guang University (attested 2016, 2026).

Chihiro Nakayashiki works in Tibetology and religious studies, holding degrees from Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific and Kyoto universities. Nakayashiki held research posts with JSPS (2014–2016, 2019–2022) and the University of Edinburgh (2019–2020), alongside various teaching posts in Japan.

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) studied religious studies at Tokyo and Kyoto universities under Bunzaburo Matsumoto. Akamatsu held professorships at Keijo Imperial University (1927–1941), Ryukoku, Hanazono, Koyasan, and Yamaguchi universities, and lectured at Kyoto and Kyushu universities.
Chijun Hamada works in Buddhist studies. Hamada held posts at Taisho University as an assistant and at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute as a researcher, both attested in 1978.

Chikafumi Watanabe specializes in Buddhist studies. Watanabe earned a master's at the University of British Columbia under Karin Preisendanz and Ashok Aklujkar, and a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura in 1995.
Chiko Corona works in Buddhist studies. Corona studied under traditional teachers Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.
Chikyo Yamamoto (1913–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Yamamoto served as a professor (attested 1970) and part-time lecturer (attested 1980) at Koyasan University.
